metadata.methods_description: Participants sat in a darkened, sound-attenuated room, viewing an LCD monitor at 152 cm, and responded with a keyboard and a headset for verbal responses. They read 180 sentences (30 each of agreement, semantic, double and word-order violations, plus 60 control sentences). Three words were shown at a time in an RSVP-with-flankers design: the white center word was flanked by grey words, each word appeared for 400 ms and slid to the right, and there was no ISI.

citation_details.title: Predicting Cognitive Tasks from Single-Channel EEG through Task-Semantic Alignment
citation_details.author: Ryota Kanai
citation_details.abstract: Studies of data scaling in electroencephalography (EEG) and related noninvasive recordings suggest that simple wearable devices could eventually reveal more about cognitive states. However, publicly available EEG data are difficult to combine. Different laboratories record different tasks, participants, and devices. Task-agnostic self-supervised learning can exploit such data, but representations learned only with EEG signals have not consistently produced feature representations that are directly effective for decoding the cognitive state. We therefore aimed to incorporate task information by embedding experimental instructions, stimuli and response demands in a common semantic space, and trained an EEG encoder to align signals from a single anterior--posterior differential channel with those task vectors.
